audits.title: Improvement in the treatment of stable ankle fractures: an audit based approach.
audits.standard: Departmental evidence-based guidelines on recognition and functional treatment of stable ankle fractures

cycle1.result: Recognition and functional treatment of stable ankle fractures was rarely followed.

audits.intervention: Introduction of formal departmental evidence-based guidelines.

cycle2.result: Subsequent audits showed progressive improvement with significant reductions in time immobilised in plaster, time non-weight bearing and number of routine check radiographs, without compromising safety.

audits.other_findings: More than two audit cycles reported; numbers not given in the abstract.
audits.citation: Wykes PR, Eccles K, Thennavan B, Barrie JL. Improvement in the treatment of stable ankle fractures: an audit based approach. Injury. 2004;35(8):799-804. doi:10.1016/s0020-1383(03)00207-9. PMID: 15246804.

audits.title: Audit of ankle injuries in an accident and emergency department.
audits.standard: Locally developed ankle injury protocol based on published reports
audits.setting: Accident and emergency department, North Tyneside General Hospital (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: 205 (80%) had radiography; 20 ligamentous injuries reviewed; 13 inappropriate fracture clinic referrals.

audits.intervention: Introduction of an ankle injury management protocol.

cycle2.result: 186 (70%) had radiography; 66 ligamentous injuries reviewed; 9 inappropriate referrals (53% reduction); protocol completed in 87% of notes.

audits.other_findings: 550 patients over four months across both phases.
audits.citation: Packer GJ, Goring CC, Gayner AD, Craxford AD. Audit of ankle injuries in an accident and emergency department. BMJ. 1991;302(6781):885-887. doi:10.1136/bmj.302.6781.885. PMID: 1902753.

audits.title: Fixation of ankle fractures - a major trauma centre's experience in improving quality.
audits.standard: Reduction criteria published by Pettrone et al.
audits.setting: Aintree University Hospital, Liverpool (major trauma centre); image intensifier films reviewed on PACS by at least two blinded observers
audits.intervention: Education and reflection between 2013 and 2015; then a change in process in ankle fracture management supported by education between 2015 and 2017.
audits.other_findings: Interim 2015 re-audit (68 patients, after education alone) showed malreduction rising to 43.8%. Final major complication rate 0.98%; deep infection 0.5%.
audits.citation: Whitehouse S, Mason LW, Jayatilaka L, Molloy AP. Fixation of ankle fractures - a major trauma centre's experience in improving quality. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2019;101(6):387-390. doi:10.1308/rcsann.2018.0098. PMID: 31155894.

audits.title: Audit changes practice-a simple education intervention can lead to better outcome in ankle fracture surgery.
audits.standard: Anatomical reduction assessed by Pettrone's radiological criteria
audits.setting: Leicester Orthopaedics, University Hospitals of Leicester

cycle1.result: Malreduced fixation in 25% of cases; inadequate restoration of fibular length was the most common malreduction.

audits.intervention: Regional teaching and dissemination of infographic posters.
audits.other_findings: No significant differences in age, gender or time to surgery between phases.
audits.citation: Kheiran A, Roberts V, Rana B, Mangwani J. Audit changes practice-a simple education intervention can lead to better outcome in ankle fracture surgery. J Clin Orthop Trauma. 2020;11(3):422-425. doi:10.1016/j.jcot.2020.03.022. PMID: 32405202.

audits.title: The acute management of ankle fractures (Augment) study: A prospective trainee led national collaborative audit of the Boast 12 guidelines.
audits.standard: BOAST 12 (BOA/BOFAS) standards for ankle fractures: documentation, imaging, management and follow-up
audits.setting: 52 UK sites, trainee-led national collaborative audit (AUGMENT)

cycle1.result: Overall BOAST 12 compliance 41.7%; neurovascular documentation 40.7%; VTE assessment 61.5%.

audits.other_findings: Compliance with all 16 BOAST 12 standards was associated with higher discharge rate by 12 weeks (p = 0.005).
audits.citation: Fennelly JT, Gourbault LJ, Stedman T, Price MJ, Ward AE, AUGMENT Collaborative. The acute management of ankle fractures (Augment) study: A prospective trainee led national collaborative audit of the Boast 12 guidelines. Surgeon. 2021;19(5):e237-e244. doi:10.1016/j.surge.2020.11.001. PMID: 33414043.

audits.title: Results From an All Wales Trainee Led Collaborative Prospective Audit on Management of Ankle Fractures.
audits.standard: BOAST guideline on management of ankle fractures (documentation, imaging including CT for posterior malleolus, weight-bearing X-rays, early weight-bearing)
audits.setting: Nine NHS hospitals across six university health boards in Wales, trainee collaborative (WORC) prospective snapshot audit

cycle1.result: Documentation: mechanism 94.4%, skin 71.3%, neurovascular status 80.1%, comorbidities 81%, alcohol 34.3%, smoking 41.7%. Mortice view 75.9%. CT for posterior malleolus fracture 15/31 (48.38%) operative and 0/9 non-operative. Weight-bearing X-ray in non-operative group 22/106 (20.8%). Early weight-bearing 63/106 (59.43%) non-operative and 11/110 (10%) operative.

audits.other_findings: Reason for delayed weight-bearing after surgery was documented in only 16/99 (16.16%). Education, an infographic and a re-audit were planned.
audits.citation: Gokhale S, D'sa P, Agarwal R, Clutton J, Roy K, Carpenter EC, et al.. Results From an All Wales Trainee Led Collaborative Prospective Audit on Management of Ankle Fractures. Cureus. 2021;13(11):e19269. doi:10.7759/cureus.19269. PMID: 34900463.

audits.title: A Clinical Audit of Orthopaedic Clinical Documentation of Acute Ankle Fractures: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: BOAST ankle fracture standards and NICE NG37: documentation of mechanism, skin integrity, circulation, neurological examination and repeat neurovascular examination after reduction; target 100%
audits.setting: Trauma and orthopaedics, single centre (audit approved at University Hospitals Dorset, Poole General Hospital; authors at Dorset County Hospital)

cycle1.result: Mechanism of injury 86%; skin integrity 54%; circulation status 54%; detailed vascular examination 17%; neurological examination 54%; sensory detail 48%; MRC motor scale 48%; repeat neurovascular examination after reduction 56%; overall precise documentation of clinical findings 17%.

audits.intervention: Targeted education on documentation standards at induction and trauma meetings, with case-based discussion reports; made a permanent part of departmental teaching.

cycle2.result: Mechanism of injury 100%; skin integrity 100%; circulation status 88%; detailed vascular examination 88%; neurological examination 88%; sensory detail 88%; MRC motor scale 88%; repeat neurovascular examination after reduction 88%; overall precise documentation 88%.

audits.other_findings: Re-audit identified 22 patients, 17 included after exclusions. The shorthand 'DNVI' was the main cause of incomplete records and persisted in two patients after the intervention.
audits.citation: Snober M, Mustafa Q. A Clinical Audit of Orthopaedic Clinical Documentation of Acute Ankle Fractures: A Quality Improvement Project. Cureus. 2023;15(11):e49001. doi:10.7759/cureus.49001. PMID: 38111391.

audits.title: A Quality Improvement Project to Measure and Improve the Quality of Below-Knee Ankle Cast Application in Emergency Departments.
audits.standard: AO Foundation guidance: ankle immobilised in neutral plantigrade position; acceptable tibia-to-sole angle 80-100 degrees on lateral radiograph
audits.setting: Urgent treatment centre and emergency departments of two district general hospitals

cycle1.result: Mean angle 108.5 degrees (SD 11.7); 18/65 (27.7%) within 80-100 degrees (DGH 1 n=32, DGH 2 n=33).

audits.intervention: Single interactive session led by plaster technicians (for UTC nurses at DGH 1 and for ED junior doctors at DGH 2) plus educational posters where plastering occurred.

cycle2.result: Mean angle 106.2 degrees (SD 11.9) (p=0.285); 23/61 (37.7%) within 80-100 degrees (p=0.231) (DGH 1 n=28, DGH 2 n=33).

audits.other_findings: Acceptable casts improved by 22% at the site that trained UTC nurses but only 3% at the site that trained junior doctors; angles were measured by a single reviewer.
audits.citation: Pritchard MW, Apostolides M, Baggott PJ, Donnelly L. A Quality Improvement Project to Measure and Improve the Quality of Below-Knee Ankle Cast Application in Emergency Departments. Cureus. 2024;16(4):e57479. doi:10.7759/cureus.57479. PMID: 38699119.

audits.title: Evaluating Compliance to Intra-operative Syndesmosis Stress Testing During Ankle Fracture Fixation: Are We Stressing It?
audits.standard: BOAST ankle fracture guidance; radiological evidence of intra-operative syndesmosis stress testing saved and documented on operation notes, target 80% each
audits.setting: Trauma unit, district general hospital, University Hospitals Dorset (Poole)

cycle1.result: Radiological evidence saved 55% (n=49); documentation on operation notes 71% (n=63); neither in 25% (n=22).

audits.intervention: Findings presented at clinical governance; poster in on-call room and theatre areas and a teaching presentation by an associate specialist foot and ankle surgeon.

cycle2.result: Radiological evidence saved 82% (n=41), p=0.001; documentation 82% (n=41), p=0.14; neither in 6% (n=3). Both targets met.

audits.other_findings: Audit did not assess the quality or technique of the stress tests, only their presence.
audits.citation: Rahim AK, Imtiaz H, Durrani A, Oo TP, Barot K, Kouklidis G, et al.. Evaluating Compliance to Intra-operative Syndesmosis Stress Testing During Ankle Fracture Fixation: Are We Stressing It?. Cureus. 2025;17(9):e92617. doi:10.7759/cureus.92617. PMID: 40980789.
